The green square is placed on this horizontal diameter, its bottom side is on the diameter, and its two upper vertices lie on the circle. Then reason: Let the side length of the square be s. The problem gives that the area of the square is 20, so s^2 = 20. Place the center of the circle at the midpoint of the horizontal diameter, then the two vertices on the upper side of the square can be regarded as coordinates (±s/2, s). They are on the circle, so the radius satisfies r^2 = (s/2)^2 + s^2 = 5s^2/4 = 5×20/4 = 25, therefore r = 5. The width of the rectangle is the diameter of the circle 2r = 10, and the height is the distance from the diameter to the point of tangency r = 5, so the area of the rectangle = 10×5 = 50 cm^2.

The green square has its bottom side on this diameter and its two top vertices on the circle. Let the square side be s. From the text, s^2=20. Because the square is centered on the vertical diameter, a radius from the circle center to a top vertex of the square forms a right triangle with horizontal leg s/2 and vertical leg s. Thus r^2=(s/2)^2+s^2=5s^2/4=25. The rectangle has width 2r and height r, so its area is 2r^2=50 cm^2.
